results.reader_title: Wellcome finds UK biomedical PhD support uneven
results.reader_what: Wellcome reports good research retention alongside inconsistent supervision, mental-health concerns and pressure to publish.
results.reader_why: Evidence informs European research-career funding and doctoral training design.
results.reader_more: The 2018 review draws on UK and Wellcome datasets, a literature review, interviews and a 2017 online survey. It reports stronger research-career retention among Wellcome cohort graduates than the biomedical PhD average. Survey respondents flagged supervision quality, scientific enquiry time, training support and mental health. Findings are descriptive and self-reported in part.

deep_analysis.research_question: How effective and supportive is UK biomedical PhD training and what should Wellcome change?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Doctoral training has expanded but supervision, mental health, research culture and training support need improvement.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Literature review, HESA datasets (2012–16), Wellcome career tracking, interviews and survey (2017).
deep_analysis.qualification: The online survey was opt-in, so wellbeing responses should not be interpreted as UK-wide prevalence estimates; comparisons do not establish causal programme effects.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Substantive European research system evidence on doctoral careers and research funding.
